questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Railway Engineering Principles & Permanent Way Components
questions.text: Explain the components and functions of a Railway Permanent Way (Rails, Sleepers, Ballast, Fastenings, Subgrade). What is Creep of Rails? Explain causes, effects, and prevention of rail creep (Anti-creepers / Rail anchors). Explain Coning of Wheels and Tilting of Rails (1 in 20).

Derive the formula for Superelevation / Cant ($e = \frac{G v^2}{127 R}$) on a curved railway track of gauge $G$. Define Equilibrium Cant, Cant Deficiency, Cant Excess, and Negative Cant. Calculate the equilibrium cant and maximum permissible speed on a $2^\circ$ Broad Gauge curved track if maximum cant deficiency is $7.6\,\text{cm}$.

Explain Gradients in railways (Ruling gradient, Momentum gradient, Pusher gradient). Why is Grade Compensation provided on railway curves? If the ruling gradient on a BG track is 1 in 200 and a $4^\circ$ curve is introduced, calculate the allowable compensated gradient (Compensation on BG $= 0.04\%$ per degree of curve).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Railway Engineering Principles & Permanent Way Components
questions.text: Draw a neat line diagram of a simple Right-Hand Turnout and label all components: Facing direction, Trailing direction, Stock rails, Tongue rails, Stretcher bar, Lead rails, Check rails, Wing rails, Point rail, Splice rail, Theoretical Nose of Crossing (TNC), and Actual Nose of Crossing (ANC).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Airport Planning, Runway Orientation & Length Corrections
questions.text: Explain aircraft characteristics affecting airport design (Weight, Wing span, Wheel base, Turning radius, Cruising speed). What is Airport Master Planning? Describe airport zoning regulations and imaginary surfaces (Primary surface, Approach surface, Transitional surface, Horizontal surface, Conical surface).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Airport Planning, Runway Orientation & Length Corrections
questions.text: Explain the Wind Rose Diagram method for determining runway orientation. Differentiate between Wind Rose Type I (Direction percentage) and Wind Rose Type II (Direction, duration, and wind velocity intensity). Explain the crosswind component limit ($15-20\,\text{km/h}$) and calculate the wind coverage ($95\%$ rule according to FAA/ICAO).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Airport Planning, Runway Orientation & Length Corrections
questions.text: The basic runway length under standard sea-level conditions is $2400\,\text{m}$. The airport site is at an elevation of $1200\,\text{m}$ above mean sea level. The reference airport temperature is $32^\circ\text{C}$ and effective runway gradient is $0.5\%$. Apply ICAO sequential corrections for: (a) Elevation ($7\%$ per $300\,\text{m}$), (b) Temperature ($1\%$ per $1^\circ\text{C}$ rise above standard temperature $T_{std} = 15 - 0.0065 E$), and (c) Gradient ($20\%$ per $1\%$ effective gradient). Check the combined elevation and temperature correction limit ($35\%$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Railway Engineering Principles & Permanent Way Components
questions.text: What is Sleeper Density ($M + x$)? Calculate the number of sleepers required for a Broad Gauge (BG) railway track of length $1024\,\text{m}$ if standard rail length is $12.8\,\text{m}$ and sleeper density is $M + 7$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Railway Engineering Principles & Permanent Way Components
questions.text: Explain Crossing Angle ($\alpha$) and Number of Crossing ($N = \cot\alpha$). Calculate the lead distance and radius of a turnout curve for a 1 in 8.5 turnout on a Broad Gauge track using Coles' method.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Railway Engineering Principles & Permanent Way Components
questions.text: Explain the objectives of Railway Signaling and Interlocking. Explain the working of Two-Aspect and Multiple-Aspect Upper Quadrant (MAUQ) color light signaling and Absolute Block System.
